reason: E1 and E2 show that a continuous B2 matrix limits ductility and that phase inversion to discrete B2 in a BCC matrix improves compressive ductility in a different RHEA (Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr) via controlled annealing. However, the cited evidence does not address HfZrTiTa0.53, tensile ductility, or the specific annealing schedule proposed, leaving key premises about the alloy and loading mode unsupported.
premises: Continuous B2 matrix causes poor ductility in RHEAs
Phase inversion to discrete B2 in BCC matrix improves ductility
Controlled annealing can achieve this phase inversion
The mechanism is reduced connectivity of brittle phase enabling dislocation motion
The specific alloy HfZrTiTa0.53 can undergo this phase inversion
